title: UPI Crosses Rs 1 Lakh Crore a Day for the First Time in Record October
excerpt: UPI processed 25.47 billion transactions worth Rs 31.53 lakh crore in October, with average daily value of Rs 1,01,707 crore — and NPCI has deferred merchant charges until after Diwali.
body:
• UPI processed a record 25.47 billion transactions in October, up 23% from a year earlier and 5.8% from September, according to National Payments Corporation of India data.
  • Transaction value reached a record Rs 31.53 lakh crore, up 16% year-on-year; average daily value crossed Rs 1 lakh crore for the first time, at Rs 1,01,707 crore.
  • October was the first month UPI passed both 25 billion transactions and Rs 30 lakh crore in value; the previous monthly value record was Rs 29.90 lakh crore in May 2026.
  • NPCI has deferred the proposed merchant discount rate on select UPI merchant transactions, originally set for October 15, until after Diwali, with the new date to be notified separately.

India's Unified Payments Interface has crossed a threshold that puts its scale in one number: in October, the average day of UPI payments was worth more than Rs 1 lakh crore. Data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) on Sunday put average daily transaction value at Rs 1,01,707 crore in October, up from Rs 97,913 crore in September, Inc42 reported.

The October numbers

UPI processed 25.47 billion transactions in October, a record, up 23% from October 2025 and 5.8% from September's 24.07 billion, according to NPCI data reported by IANS. The value of those transactions was Rs 31.53 lakh crore, up 16% year-on-year and 7.4% month-on-month. Because October has 31 days to September's 30, the daily averages are the cleaner comparison: daily volume rose to 822 million transactions from 802 million, and daily value rose 3.9% on Inc42's calculation. October was the first month above both 25 billion transactions and Rs 30 lakh crore in value; the previous monthly value record, Rs 29.90 lakh crore, was set in May 2026.

What drove it

The festive season is the explanation the industry itself offers. Cashfree co-founder Reeju Datta said the festive season, including Navratri and major online sales, played a key role in driving the increase, according to Data Street. October's calendar — Navratri, Dussehra and the run-up to Diwali on November 8 — concentrates India's heaviest retail weeks into a single month, and UPI, run by NPCI since 2016, is now the default way those purchases are paid for.

The deferred merchant charge

The record month lands just before a change in how UPI makes money. NPCI had planned to introduce a merchant discount rate — a fee on certain person-to-merchant UPI transactions — from October 15. That rollout has been deferred until after Diwali; NPCI said its UPI and Services Steering Committee postponed it keeping the festive season in mind, and the revised implementation date will be notified separately. For merchants and payment companies, October's record volumes strengthen both sides of that argument: the system's scale is the case for monetising it, and its festive peak is the reason not to change the rules mid-season.

What to watch next

Two dates matter now: NPCI's announcement of the new merchant-discount-rate start date, expected after Diwali, and the November figures in early December, which will show how much of October's record was festival demand and how much is the new baseline. On daily averages, the baseline question is precise — whether average daily value holds above Rs 1 lakh crore in a month without a festival in it.
nri_angle: For NRIs who send money home and pay family bills through UPI-linked accounts, the deferred merchant-discount-rate rollout is the item to watch after Diwali.
author: Diaspora Desk
